quote_found: We investigated treatment-covariate interactions on prespecified baseline covariates. No strong evidence of subgroup effects was observed for other baseline covariates.
what_is_wrong: The detailed characterization of Wei 2018 is accurate: it fitted separate PCOS and ovulatory models, reported P<0.001 for the two PCOS treatment-by-response interactions, found no significant corresponding interactions in ovulatory women, and did not report a pooled treatment-by-PCOS-status test. The word “only” is now false, however. A completed INFORM IPD meta-analysis preprint was posted on SSRN on 29 June 2026 under the same prospective registration, CRD42021296566. It formally investigated prespecified treatment-covariate interactions across 13 trials (9060 participants); its protocol explicitly prespecified PCOS/WHO group II anovulation as a participant-level treatment-covariate interaction. Thus Wei 2018 is no longer the only source formally modeling interactions with data spanning these trial populations.

what_is_wrong: The two pooled RR estimates and confidence intervals do appear in the source, but the live-birth sample sizes printed beside them are internally impossible and assigned to the wrong populations. Table II identifies the three high-responder live-birth trials as Absalan (100), Chen (1508), and Aflatoonian (280), totaling 1888—not 3398. It identifies the three normal-responder live-birth trials as Coates (179), Shi (2157), and Vuong (782), totaling 3118—not 1608. The article separately states that all four high-responder RCTs total only 2010 participants and all four normal-responder RCTs total 3255. In addition, no cross-stratum interaction test was performed, so “a difference in precision, not in effect size” is an interpretation of similar point estimates, not a tested source result.

what_is_wrong: The protocol quotation is accurate, but the time-sensitive assertion that only the protocol has been published is obsolete. A 29-page INFORM results preprint, “Frozen Versus Fresh Embryo Transfer in IVF – An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials (INFORM),” was posted on SSRN on 29 June 2026 and cites PROSPERO CRD42021296566. It reports 13 trials and 9060 randomized participants, an adjusted RR for live birth after first transfer of 1.00 (95% CI 0.86 to 1.17), formal prespecified treatment-covariate analyses, a nonlinear progesterone interaction, and no strong evidence of subgroup effects for the other baseline covariates. The abstract does not print a standalone PCOS/ovulatory-status interaction P value, but the categorical claim that there is still no INFORM results report or IPD interaction analysis is false.
